name: Soups, broths, and stocks (canned, dry-mix, bouillon, RTD carton)
native_basis_label: as consumed / ready-to-serve (reconstituted to serving strength; dry-mix and bouillon assessed as prepared, not as the concentrate)
scope_note: Canned soups, dry soup mixes, bouillon cubes and powders, and ready-to-drink carton stocks and broths, plant- or meat-based. Assessed on an as-consumed (reconstituted-to-serving) basis: a bouillon cube is evaluated as the prepared broth, not as the concentrated cube, because there is no legislated concentrate-to-serving ratio. Bone broth is certified separately under row bone-broth. Composite method identical to mixed meals; canned tin is genuinely material here (canned soup).
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; COMPOSITE — disclosed read-across from strictest applicable principal-component sovereign ML; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.basis: read-across from strictest applicable principal-component Pb ML (as consumed)

components.basis: food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule; source unit mg/kg

Pb.label: vegetable and meat components (both 100 ug/kg) are the strictest applicable lead anchors for stock/broth HK (Cap 132V) admitted to the credible set (2026-08-17); its vegetable-component ML is the strictest applicable and binds.

Cd.basis: read-across from strictest applicable principal-component Cd ML (as consumed)
Cd.label: legume soups (lentil, split-pea, bean) make the EU pulse cadmium ML (40 ug/kg) the binding component

tAs.basis: read-across from the cereal-grain total-arsenic ML (as consumed)

components.basis: food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule; source unit mg/kg

tAs.label: cereal grains carry the only credible-regulator total-arsenic ML among the components; the toxic inorganic fraction is controlled on the iAs cell HK (Cap 132V) admitted to the credible set (2026-08-17); its vegetable-component ML is the strictest applicable and binds.
tAs.substantiation: Total arsenic is a screen; inorganic arsenic (iAs cell, 100 ug/kg) controls the toxic species. Cereal-grain tAs ML (FSANZ, 1000 ug/kg) is the applicable credible component anchor.

iAs.basis: read-across from strictest applicable inorganic-arsenic component ML (as consumed)
iAs.label: seafood and rice components make inorganic arsenic material; EU fish iAs ML (100) binds, stricter than milled rice (150)

tHg.basis: read-across from the seafood total-mercury ML (as consumed)

components.basis: food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule; source unit mg/kg

tHg.label: mercury is material only in seafood-based soups (bisque, chowder), which inherit the EU seafood mercury ceiling (500 ug/kg) HK (Cap 132V) admitted to the credible set (2026-08-17); its vegetable-component ML is the strictest applicable and binds.
tHg.substantiation: No credible regulator sets a mercury ML for terrestrial-meat or vegetable stock; a seafood bisque or chowder inherits the Category 6 seafood mercury ceiling (EU 2023/915, 500 ug/kg). Methylmercury bounded by this total-mercury ceiling.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is measured present in soup, broth, or stock products in the routed corpus (hwang2022, 480 home-meal-replacement products by direct mercury analyzer; authors2025, ICP-MS/speciation), and a prepared soup, broth, or stock can carry a seafood component that is a genuine methylmercury pathway. It is therefore NOT declared not-material; it is held under mandatory analytical control (measured every lot, reflex speciation) and bounded by the total-mercury cell (MeHg <= tHg).
MeHg.reference_method: Methylmercury by HPLC-ICP-MS / direct mercury analyzer on an elevated total-mercury result; screened, bounded by the tHg cell.

Ni.basis: read-across from strictest applicable nickel component ML (EU 2024/1252, as consumed)
Ni.label: fruiting-vegetable component carries the strictest EU nickel ML (400 ug/kg); Tier-2 analyte

Sn.basis: canned-foods tin maximum level (Codex CXS 193), directly applicable to canned soup
Sn.label: Canned soup is a canned food and is directly governed by the canned-foods tin ML (Codex CXS 193, 250 mg/kg). Dry-mix, bouillon, and RTD-carton forms have no tin migration pathway; the ML binds the canned form.
Sn.substantiation: The canned-foods tin ML is a DIRECT sovereign limit on the canned form (regulatory-alignment), not a component read-across. Non-canned soup forms (carton RTD, dry mix, bouillon) have no tinplate contact and no tin source; total tin is reported and any non-canned signal triggers packaging investigation.

Al.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium maximum level for soups, stocks, or their food components. Reported as an investigate-the-line screen (cookware, packaging, additives).
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS; screen, not a health limit.

Cr.basis: read-across from the strictest applicable total-chromium component ML (as consumed)

components.basis: food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule; source unit mg/kg

Cr.label: Hong Kong Cap 132V sets a total-chromium ML of 500 ug/kg for vegetables other than pulses; a prepared composite with a vegetable component reads across it. Total chromium is a screen — the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), controlled on the Cr-VI cell.
Cr.substantiation: HK Cap 132V Part 2 total-chromium schedule, Vegetables other than pulses = 500 ug/kg. No credible regulator sets a total-chromium ML for a prepared meal itself; HK's vegetable component ML is the strictest applicable anchor now that HK is in the credible-regulator set.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is reduced to Cr-III in a cooked, wet, organic-rich matrix; a Cr-VI result in soup or broth is an artifact of the total-chromium screen, not real exposure. No credible regulator sets a Cr-VI food ML.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Cr-VI not measured routinely; total chromium (Cr cell) bounds any hexavalent fraction.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible regulator sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food; Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in a cooked, wet, organic-rich matrix and any Cr(VI) signal is an artifact of the total-chromium screen. Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA; FSANZ; Health Canada; UK; HK Cap 132V — none set a hexavalent-chromium content limit for food.
